To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single 3S WBMR protocol can be sufficient for the investigation of most paediatric conditions.
a single 3T 3D STIIR sequence is sufficient to investigate a broad range of common paediatric pathologies.
a single 3S sequence is sufficient in the majority of cases, but not in all, and that the PPV is dependent on the type of pathology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the feasibility of a single 2D T2-Weight MRI sequence for the investigation of the most common paediatric conditions.
the use of a single STIR sequence as the sole sequence for WB-MRI, in the investigation of common paediatric conditions.
a single 3T WB MRI in paediatric patients with different pathologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D IR STIR sequence alone is sufficient to investigate the majority of common pediatric conditions.
3D IR-STIR is sufficient for the majority of indications, but that the addition of other sequences (T1W, DWI) is useful in some specific cases.
3D STI alone is sufficient for the investigation of common paediatric conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3D STIRS alone can be sufficient to diagnose common paediatric pathologies with a sensitivity of 81% and a PPV >85%.
3D-STIR alone can be sufficient for the diagnosis of child abuse, chronic recurrent multifocal ostemyelitis and lymphoma.
a 3D-STIR alone could be used in a clinical setting, but that the 3S sequence is more sensitive in detecting lymphomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a 3D T2-weighted sequence alone is as sensitive as a Whole-body MRI (WBMR) protocol including diffusion weighted, T1- and STIR 2D sequences in a pediatric population, and that the 3D T1-weighted sequence is not needed.

a 3D IR-STIR sequence alone can be sufficient for investigating the common paediatric conditions in children, as long as the radiologist is familiar with the typical imaging appearance of the disease and has a high index of suspicion.
a single STIR sequence can be used for the investigation of most paediatric conditions, with the possible exception of lymphoma and neuroblastic tumours.
